notes: Craft knowledge for the interpretation layer (js/taste/interpret.js). Each quality names a visual or literary effect that a combination of vocabulary terms produces, with a neutral explanation of how those techniques work together. A quality is mentioned only when the person's own findings contain at least `min` of its `members` in the same direction; the explanation describes the technique, never the person. Edit freely: the statistics never read this file.

cinema.name: chiaroscuro
cinema.explains: Hard, directional light in a mostly dark frame sculpts form: faces and objects emerge from shadow, and the darkness becomes part of the composition rather than an absence of light.

cinema.name: graphic light
cinema.explains: Light that takes visible shapes, such as stripes from blinds, beams in the air or the outline of a rim, becomes a drawn element of the frame as well as a way of seeing.

cinema.name: soft, even light
cinema.explains: Diffuse light with gentle shadows lets the whole scene read evenly. Nothing is singled out by the lighting, so attention goes to arrangement, place and gesture.

cinema.name: composed symmetry
cinema.explains: A centred subject in a balanced frame makes an image feel deliberate and placed, closer to a tableau than a glimpse; small departures from symmetry then read strongly.

cinema.name: scale and space
cinema.explains: Wide frames with figures small against land, sky or architecture put the weight on place and scale; empty space carries as much of the image as the subject.

cinema.name: closeness
cinema.explains: Close framing and shallow focus separate a face or object from its surroundings, so expression and surface carry the image and the background becomes a soft field.

cinema.name: staging in depth
cinema.explains: With near and far planes both sharp and figures placed at several distances, the eye travels through the frame and reads relationships between foreground and background.

cinema.name: frames within frames
cinema.explains: Doorways, windows and foreground objects frame the subject a second time, which makes looking itself part of the image and often suggests separation or watching.

cinema.name: designed colour
cinema.explains: Strong colour used as structure, such as a single dominant hue, a deliberate contrast or one vivid accent, lets colour carry mood and direct the eye rather than merely record the scene.

cinema.name: a warm palette
cinema.explains: Neighbouring warm hues (ambers, oranges, golds) give light a tactile, lamp-lit or sunlit quality and bind the frame into one colour family.

cinema.name: a cool palette
cinema.explains: Blues and teals cool the image and often push it towards night, distance or reserve.

cinema.name: tonal black and white
cinema.explains: Without colour the image is built from tone alone: the range from black to white, and the texture within it, does the work that colour would.

cinema.name: visible atmosphere
cinema.explains: Smoke, mist or dust in the air catches light and softens distance, so the space between camera and subject becomes visible volume.

cinema.name: backlight and silhouette
cinema.explains: Light from behind reduces figures to outline. Shape, posture and gesture matter more than detail, and the light source itself can become the subject.

cinema.name: momentum
cinema.explains: Diagonals and movement caught mid-action give a frame forward energy; the image feels like a moment taken from a continuous action.

cinema.name: stillness
cinema.explains: Stillness, spare composition and restrained colour slow the image down; small details and the relation between a figure and empty space take on weight.

cinema.name: drawn worlds
cinema.explains: In hand-drawn animation light, colour and texture are painted rather than captured: skies, water and interiors can be shaped entirely to the mood of the scene.

cinema.name: the returned gaze
cinema.explains: A figure looking into the lens breaks the usual invisibility of the camera and addresses the viewer directly.

literature.name: restraint
literature.explains: Plain words and few figures of speech leave feeling unstated; the reader infers what the prose declines to say, so small details carry a great deal.

literature.name: lyrical prose
literature.explains: Long, cadenced sentences, repetition and dense imagery let rhythm and sound carry feeling; the prose is meant to be heard as much as followed.

literature.name: formal experiment
literature.explains: Broken syntax, unmarked speech and blurred boundaries between narrator and character make the reader assemble the scene, so form becomes part of the meaning.

literature.name: a close voice
literature.explains: A first-person voice that speaks to someone, or looks back on itself, makes the passage feel confided rather than told.

literature.name: scenic immediacy
literature.explains: Present action at the speed it happens, with exact physical detail, puts the reader inside the moment rather than above it.

literature.name: reflection and digression
literature.explains: Digression and qualification let thought wander and return; the pleasure is in the movement of a mind more than in events.
